_comment: Second booth pool. lines.py merges every JSON in this folder by key, so
these EXTEND the pools in booth.json rather than replacing them.
Split into a second file purely so the first stays readable.
Weighted toward the highest-traffic categories — overtake, battle and
the analyst's colour — because those are what a long race exhausts.

overtake.t: {a} pounces! Past {b}!
There it is — {a} clears {b}.
{b} covered the inside and {a} went the other way!
{a} sends it! And it works!
Switchback! {a} comes out ahead!
{a} was never lifting there. Past {b}.
A dummy from {a}, and {b} buys it completely!
Clean as you like — {a} takes {pos}.
{b} ran a fraction wide and {a} was waiting.
That's patience rewarded from {a}.
Two wheels on the grass, but {a} makes it stick!
{a} threw it up the inside and {b} had to yield.
Superb from {a}. {b} did nothing wrong.
{a} is through, and there was contact!
Brave. Very brave. And {a} has {pos}.
{b} defended once, defended twice, and lost it anyway.
{a} had the traction and that was the difference.
Muscled through! {a} was not going to be denied!
{a} slices past {b} without breaking stride.
The tow did the work — {a} is by.
Rear wing open, and {a} is gone.
No electronics to help there — just {a} out-braking {b}.

battle.t: {a} and {b}, and there is nothing in it.
{a} has a look, {b} shuts the door.
{gap}. That is all that separates them.
{b} is defending like his race depends on it.
This is the fight of the race right now.
{a} is looking everywhere for a way past {b}.
They have been like this for three corners.
{a} tried the inside, no way through.
Something has to give between these two.
{b} knows exactly where {a} wants to go.

closing.t: {a} has the bit between his teeth — {gap}.
Four tenths a lap, and {gap} to find.
{b} is not going to like what he sees in his mirrors.
That gap was two seconds. Now it is {gap}.

pulling_away.t: Nobody has an answer. {gap} the margin.
{drv} has simply driven away from the field.

fastlap.t: And that is the fastest lap of the race so far.

spin.t: Snap oversteer, and {drv} is a passenger!
No traction control to save him there.

offtrack.t: A lock-up and a long lap for {drv}.
Across the kerbs and into the run-off.

pit.t: {drv} takes the stop, and rejoins in traffic.

retire.t: Smoke, and {drv} is coasting to a halt.
That's a cruel way for {drv} to end it.

recovery.t: {drv} has been superb since that setback — {pos}.
From the back of the pack to {pos}. Some drive.

traffic.t: Backmarkers ahead, and this could be pivotal.
{drv} has to pick his way through now.
Blue flags out for the leaders.
Lapped cars between {drv} and clean air.

standings.t: As it stands: {drv}, {b}, and the rest.

final_laps.t: {laps} to go, and nothing is settled.

lastlap.t: Final lap! Everything on the line!
This is it — the last time around!
One lap. One lap for everything.

win.t: Across the line — {drv}, the winner at {trk}!
{drv} has done it! Brilliant from start to finish!
And it is {drv} who takes the flag!

analysis.t: Watch his hands. Barely a correction all lap.
He's short-shifting to protect the rears. Smart.
That's a driver who knows exactly what he has left.
The car's moving around a lot on entry. He's fighting it.
He's giving up a tenth a lap to save the tyre. Right call.
Line's completely different to everyone else through there.
You can hear him lifting earlier than he was ten laps ago.
That's not a setup problem, that's a confidence problem.
He's putting the car exactly where he wants it. Every lap the same.
Brake bias must be moving around on him.

analysis_era.t: A car like this bit you the moment you relaxed.
The data these teams have now is extraordinary. It used to be feel and hope.
On the ovals this is where you'd be looking for a push. Different game on a road course.
Restarts are where these races are won. Everything before is positioning.
Dirty air on a big track like this is brutal. You just can't follow.
Deployment maps, energy harvesting — I'd have needed an engineering degree.
Ground effect changed how close you can run. Night and day.
Turbo lag in these was savage. You'd get on the throttle a corner early.
Grooved tyres. Nobody liked them and everybody had to use them.
No seatbelt worth the name, no run-off. Brave men.
Same car, same engine, same tyre for all of them. Whatever you see out there is the driver.
There is nowhere to hide in a series like this. You cannot blame the machinery when the man beside you has an identical one.
The margins are absurd in these cars. Half a tenth is four or five places on a grid this tight.
Everybody here is used to being the quickest driver they know. That is the adjustment, not the lap time.
Track position is everything, because you can see the traffic building before the lap even starts.
These cars want commitment through a corner. Ease off in the middle and the aerodynamics stop working for you.
Tyre temperature is the whole art of a lap like that. A degree either side of the window and it is gone.
Nobody out there is guessing any more. Every one of them has been told exactly where the lap time is before they left the garage.
Kerbs are part of the racing line now, and they are also how you break a car. Every driver picks his own compromise.
The gap between a good lap and their best is tiny at this level, which is exactly why one mistake costs so much.
No wings, no downforce, no help. Everything you see here is throttle, brake and where he puts the kart.
Momentum is the whole thing in a kart. Scrub the speed off in the middle of a corner and you spend the next straight paying for it.
Every driver on a Formula One grid learned to race in one of these. It is the purest version of the job.
You feel a kart through your back rather than through your hands. There is nothing between the driver and the road.
Bodywork contact is part of karting in a way it never is further up. That does not make it clumsy - it makes it close.
A GT car has weight to manage that a single-seater does not. Braking is where the good ones make their money.
These are cars built to be driven for hours by more than one driver, and you can feel that compromise in every corner.
Traffic is the story in this category. Half of the skill is what a driver does with cars that are not racing him.
A car with a roof moves around under you far more than the lap times suggest. Nothing about that is tidy.
Front-wheel drive punishes greed. Ask for too much too early and it simply runs wide.
Aerodynamics matter more in these than people expect, and the moment you lose the air off the car in front you feel it.

strategy.t: Whoever stops first hands the other one clean air.
He needs to build four seconds before the stop or he comes out behind.
Track position over tyre life here. You can't pass at this circuit.
There's a stop coming. You can see it in the lap times.
Two-stopper is quicker on paper. Doesn't help you in traffic.
Fuel number's going to decide this, not the tyres.

verdict.t: Nothing wrong with that. Hard but fair.
He had to yield. Simple as that.
A touch optimistic, but he made it work.
That was the only place on the circuit he could have done it.
Textbook. Set it up a corner earlier and take it.
He'll get a look at that one from the stewards.
Both of them left room. That's how it should be done.

praise.t: That is a seriously good piece of driving.
{drv} is making this look far easier than it is.
He hasn't put a wheel wrong all afternoon.
That's the lap of the race, for my money.

criticism.t: He's overdriving it. Trying too hard.
That's going to cost him more than the place.
Too greedy on entry, and the car let go.
{drv} has thrown away a good result there.

milestone.t: Lap {lap}, and the race is beginning to settle.
Lap {lap} of {trk}, and the tyres are the story now.

session.t: {trk} it is, and the {series} field is ready.
A full grid at {trk}, and we are moments away.
Here at {trk}, this should be a good one.

restart.t: The pack is released! Racing again!
Clear track, green flag, and it is on!

green_again.t: Yellows are gone — we are racing again.
Green flags. The track is clear.
That caution is over, and it's back to green.

yellow.t: Yellows in sector — careful through there.

podium.t: {drv} takes {pos} and a place on the podium.
